title: Dry ① 수도 단수
theme_ko: 수도가 끊긴 순간 — 가뭄이 새 국면에 들다

sentences.english: The kitchen tap makes strange sounds. It coughs. It spits once, and then goes silent.

grammar.note: 앞 명사 the tap을 받는 대명사

sentences.english: “Mom,” I shout out into the living room, “water is not coming out.”
“Alyssa, shush!” Mom says.
She is watching the TV, where a news anchor is talking about the “flow crisis.”

grammar.note: 콤마 뒤 계속적 용법 — 앞 명사 the TV를 보충설명

sentences.english: This is what the media has been calling the drought ever since people got tired of hearing the word “drought.”

grammar.note: has been calling — 계속되어 온 호칭

sentences.english: Now the crisis is entering a new stage. We have no running water out of the tap.

title: Dry ② 사재기 인파
theme_ko: 물을 사재기하는 몰의 군중 — 생필품이 된 물

sentences.english: “To the mall!” says Uncle Basil. My little brother Garrett and I jump in our uncle’s truck.
As we pull into the parking lot, we can see the crowd.
“You two go in. I’ll meet you inside,” Uncle Basil says.
Inside it’s like Black Friday at its worst — but today it’s not televisions and video games people are after.

grammar.note: it’s not ~ (that) people are after — 관계사 생략
like Black Friday at its worst

sentences.english: What I see in the carts in the checkout line are mostly water bottles. The essentials of life.

grammar.note: The essentials of life = water bottles

sentences.english: There is a look of impatience on the faces of the people in line. There is even hostility, hidden by a thin layer of politeness. Even that politeness is stretched thin.

title: Dry ③ 마지막 생수
theme_ko: 빈 진열대에서 찾은 마지막 생수, 그러나 눈앞에서 빼앗기다

sentences.english: As I approach the back of the store for water bottles, I realize I am too late. The shelves are already empty.

grammar.note: I realize (that) I am ~ — 명사절 that 생략

sentences.english: I manage my way to the side aisle, trying my luck. Sometimes people place unwanted items in the wrong shelves.
Lucky! I find a single case of water that someone abandoned there maybe yesterday, when it wasn’t such a precious commodity.

grammar.note: water that someone abandoned — 목적격 that

sentences.english: I reach for it, only to find it pulled away at the last second by a woman.

grammar.note: find it pulled away — 수동 의미의 분사

sentences.english: She stacks it on top of her cart like a crown on top of her canned goods.

title: Dry ④ 거절당한 호의
theme_ko: 지난주 베푼 호의를 상기시켜도 끝내 거절당하는 아이러니

sentences.english: “I’m sorry, but we were here first,” she says.

grammar.note: “~,” she says — 인용부호 속 실제 발화

sentences.english: And then her daughter steps forward — a girl I recognize from soccer — Hali Hartling.

grammar.note: — a girl I recognize from soccer — 로 daughter를 부연
a girl (whom) I recognize — 목적격 관계대명사 생략

sentences.english: As her mother pulls their cart away, Hali leans closer to me. “I’m sorry about that, Alyssa.”
“Didn’t I share my water with you at the practice last week?” I point out to her. “Maybe you could return the favor and share a few bottles with me.”

grammar.note: could return — 완곡한 제안 '~할 수도 있잖아'

sentences.english: She looks back to her mother, who’s already moving down the aisle, then turns back to me shaking her head.

grammar.note: her mother, who’s already moving — 선행사 보충설명

sentences.english: And then she gets a little bit red in the face, and turns to leave before it becomes a deep flush.

title: Dry ⑤ 얼음이라는 기지
theme_ko: 얼음을 물 대신 확보하는 화자의 기지

sentences.english: I look for Garrett, whom I find in the frozen aisle. Then I see something.
Just past the frozen vegetables and ice cream, there is a case packed with ice. I open the door and reach for a bag.
“What are you doing? We need water, not ice,” he reminds me.
“Ice is water. Just help me,” I tell him.

grammar.note: 'Just help me'는 명령문 — 주어 you 생략

sentences.english: Garrett and I put one bag of ice after another into our cart, until it is piled as high as it can get.

grammar.note: '가능한 한 높이' — as high as it can get

sentences.english: By now other people have taken notice and begin to empty the ice case.

grammar.note: have taken notice — 방금까지 벌어진 일

title: Dry ⑥ 낯선 남자의 호의
theme_ko: 호의를 가장해 얼음을 가로채려는 낯선 남자

sentences.english: The cart is ridiculously heavy now, and almost impossible to push. Then, a man in a business suit comes up behind us. He smiles.

grammar.note: '거의 밀 수 없을 만큼' — almost impossible to push

sentences.english: “Looks like you could use some help.” He doesn’t wait for us to answer before grabbing the cart’s handle.
“Thank you for helping us,” I tell him.
“Not a problem. We all need to help one another.” He smiles again, and I return the smile.
It is good to know that difficult times can bring out the best in people. I decide that one favor deserves another.

grammar.note: It is good to know ~ — 진주어 to know

sentences.english: “Why don’t you take a bag of ice for yourself,” I suggest.
His smile does not fade. “I have a better idea,” he says. “Why don’t you take a bag of ice for yourselves, and I’ll keep the rest.”

title: Dry ⑦ 위기와 구원
theme_ko: 미소 뒤에 숨은 위협과 때맞춘 삼촌의 등장

sentences.english: For a moment I think he is joking, but then realize he is serious. “Excuse me?”

grammar.note: I think (that) he is joking — 접속사 that 생략

sentences.english: He is still smiling, but his eyes scare me.
As long as his hands are firmly locked on the handle of our cart, there is nothing to prove that it’s ours and not his.
“Is there a problem here?” It is Uncle Basil. He has arrived just in time.
“Not at all.” The man looks at the ice with a bitter face, then leaves.

title: Dry ⑧ 작품 소개·경고
theme_ko: 소설 「Dry」 소개와 물 부족이 현실이 될 수 있다는 경고

sentences.english: The above is a shortened version of the opening of the novel Dry (2018).
It tells the story of a girl who has to make tough choices for her family during a disastrous California drought.
Her unwanted adventure ends when the water supply resumes and life is back to normal.

Provided that the factors contributing to water shortages worldwide are not addressed, including climate change, population growth, and using too much water for agriculture, it is possible that this story can become a reality.

grammar.note: it is possible that ~ 의 it

sentences.english: In the summer of 2022, during the worst drought in 500 years in Europe, a stone known as a “hunger stone” was found in a Czech town along the Elbe River.

grammar.note: known as a 'hunger stone'이 앞 stone을 수식

sentences.english: The stone had a sentence written on it that read: “If you see me, then cry.”

grammar.note: written on it = 그 위에 새겨진(수식)

sentences.english: The hunger stones, found in rivers across central Europe, typically remain underwater.

grammar.note: found in rivers ~ 가 The hunger stones를 수식

sentences.english: However, when droughts occur and water levels retreat, these stones become visible.

grammar.note: droughts occur and water levels retreat

sentences.english: The stones are significant because they bear records of the past severe droughts.
Droughts cause reduced harvests, food shortages, and hunger, especially for the poor.

grammar.note: reduced harvests, food shortages, and hunger 나열

sentences.english: The words on the hunger stones are believed to warn of these hardships and to urge people to be prepared.
Considering the continuation of climate change, experts warn that the situation we face is not just a simple, occasional drought but a severe drought that could persist for decades.

grammar.note: not just A but B = A가 아니라 B

sentences.english: The United Nations has predicted that by 2050, 75 percent of the global population could suffer from the effects of drought unless significant action is taken to address climate change.
